- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially <0.33) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Lagged price movements are overpredicted — model reacts too slowly to recent sentiment shifts, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a price spike, model often overcorrects downward — forecast dips too aggressively, missing subsequent recovery.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to historical mean too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early 2025 (e.g., Example 3) when sentiment is strong and volatility is high — adjust for higher variance.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, reduce forecast magnitude — model tends to average out sentiment noise rather than reacting to directional signals.
